description.narrative: State-level strategic implementation plan of Odisha and Andhra Pradesh for the World Bank assisted Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership (RAMP) programme of Government of India focuses on formalisation of enterprises, productivity and digitalisation, and greening of MSMEs in India. Publication of the study on Enabling Environment for Sustainable Enterprises (EESE) to facilitate transition to formalization in Odisha; and Publication of a study on FDI and private sector-led local development strategies for sustainable growth and more and better-quality jobs. Findings from the study shared in regional policy discussion for evidence-based policy making, and in design of MSME support programme.

description.narrative: Tripartite Constituents collaborated in the conceptualization, development and organization of the The 3rd UN Forum on Business and Human Rights. Tripartite constituents co-organized an awareness raising on the Multinational Enterprises (MNE) Declaration for Tripartite constituents. Workers Information and Support Centre (WISC) established in State of Andhra Pradesh (AP). Odisha Food processing policy and MSME policy reflects more and better quality job creation. State Government of Odisha and AP have agreed to embed SIYB training in their state Entrepreneurship Development Programmes (EDPs). State Government of Kerala proposes to set up SIYB business solution counters in incubation centres operated by state-run Kerala Institute of Entrepreneurship Development in various districts to offer management support to budding entrepreneurs. ILO provided technical resources, developed concept note for Forum and led Technical Sessions. Co-organised session on “Protecting migrant workers during recruitment and upon return”. Also organised a session on “Pathways towards integrated approaches towards formalization”. It reflected on challenges to upholding human rights in business operations in informal economy and what could be meaningful ways to address them based on ILO Recommendation 2015 (No. 204), ILO Tripartite Declaration of Principles concerning Multinational Enterprises and Social Policy (MNE Declaration) and UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGPs).Co- organised training on “Introduction to the UNGPs and MNE Declaration” to introduce participants to the three pillars of the UNGPs and principles of the MNE Declaration.In both cases, tripartite constituents were actively involved in the discussions. More than 1000 workers especially women and migrants engaged as contract workers in MSMEs in Vishakhapatnam district supported by WISC to access various social security schemes and register in e-shram portal, alongside awareness building on workers’ rights. 200 women from disadvantaged communities have been enabled to start or formalise business and transformed into womenpreneurs. Many first-generation household income contributors, these women led businesses also provide direct employment to 1500 women and estimated indirect employment to 800 persons. 20 MSMEs engaging 3800 employees (80% women) outreached and influenced to adopt responsible management practises for improving working conditions and productivity. Awareness and capacity of 450 MSMEs enhanced on labour law compliance and sourcing practises of lead buyers to facilitate integration in supply chain. ILC 2007 Conclusions on Promotion of Sustainable Enterprises reflected in the formulation and revision of Odisha policy on MSME, Odisha Policy on Food Processing, Andhra Pradesh MSME action plan, and National MSME policy.
